answers.how: Measured Callisto's average orbital speed in 854x480 pixels (radius 182.7 px, angular displacement 0.508 rad over 3.30 s, giving 28.12 px/s) to establish the scale of 0.0223 m/px from the prior of 0.627 m/s. Measured the diameter of the Callisto model dot as ~5.8 px in 854x480 coordinates, converting to 0.13 m.

Using the scale of 0.0223 m/px (in 854x480 coordinates) derived from Callisto's orbital speed of 0.627 m/s, measured the diameter of the central Jupiter model disk as 74 px (from x=390 to x=464 and y=203 to y=277), giving 1.65 m.

Tracked the Io model from Frame 0 (t=0.000s) to Frame 99 (t=3.300s) around the center (427, 240) at an average orbital radius of 69.3 px through an angular displacement of 224.6 degrees (3.920 rad), giving an arc length of 271.7 px (82.3 px/s). Scaling by Callisto's speed (28.12 px/s = 0.627 m/s) yields 1.84 m/s.

Tracked the Europa model from Frame 0 (t=0.000s) to Frame 99 (t=3.300s) at an orbital radius of 89.2 px through an angular displacement of 111.9 degrees (1.953 rad), giving an arc length of 174.2 px (52.8 px/s). Scaling by Callisto's speed (28.12 px/s = 0.627 m/s) yields 1.18 m/s.

Tracked the Ganymede model from Frame 0 (t=0.000s) to Frame 99 (t=3.300s) at an orbital radius of 119.9 px through an angular displacement of 54.67 degrees (0.954 rad), giving an arc length of 114.4 px (34.67 px/s). Scaling by Callisto's speed (28.12 px/s = 0.627 m/s) yields 0.773 m/s.
Using the scale of 0.0223 m/px (in 854x480 coordinates) derived from Callisto's speed prior, measured the diameter of the Io model dot as ~5.6 px, converting to 0.125 m.
Using the scale of 0.0223 m/px (in 854x480 coordinates) derived from Callisto's speed prior, measured the diameter of the Europa model dot as ~6.0 px, converting to 0.135 m.
Using the scale of 0.0223 m/px (in 854x480 coordinates) derived from Callisto's speed prior, measured the diameter of the Ganymede model dot as ~6.3 px, converting to 0.14 m.

Measured the orbital diameter of Io (innermost orbit) as 138 px in 854x480 coordinates (from x=359 to x=495 for the circle and 139.6 px from tracked positions) and multiplied by the scale of 0.0223 m/px to get 3.08 m.

Measured the orbital diameter of Europa (second orbit) as 178.4 px in 854x480 coordinates (from x=338.5 to x=515.5 for the circle and R=89.2 px from tracked positions) and multiplied by the scale of 0.0223 m/px to get 3.98 m.
Measured the orbital diameter of Ganymede (third orbit) as 240 px in 854x480 coordinates (from x=307 to x=547, y=120 to y=360) and multiplied by the scale of 0.0223 m/px to get 5.35 m.
Measured the orbital diameter of Callisto (outermost orbit) as 365.4 px in 854x480 coordinates (from x=244 to x=610, y=57 to y=423) and multiplied by the scale of 0.0223 m/px to get 8.15 m.
